# Judith Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 11

---

**1** Holofernes said to her, "Take courage, woman; do not be afraid in your heart. For I have never harmed anyone who chose to serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of all the earth.

**2** And now, if your people in the hill country had not despised me, I would not have raised my spear against them. But they brought this upon themselves.

**3** Now tell me: why did you flee from them and come to us? You have come to safety. Take courage — you will live this night and from now on.

**4** No one will harm you. You will be treated well, as they treat the servants of my lord King Nebuchadnezzar."

**5** Judith said to him, "Accept the words of your servant, and let your handmaid speak freely in your presence. I will speak no falsehood to my lord this night.

**6** If you follow the words of your handmaid, God will bring through you a perfect work to completion, and my lord will not fall short of his purposes.

**7** As Nebuchadnezzar the king of all the earth lives, and as his power lives — who sent you to set every living soul in order — not only do human beings serve him through you, but the beasts of the field, the cattle, and the birds of heaven will live by your strength, under Nebuchadnezzar and all his household.

**8** For we have heard of your wisdom and the cunning of your mind; it has been declared throughout all the earth that you alone are worthy in the whole kingdom, mighty in knowledge, and admirable in the arts of war.

**9** Now concerning the word that Achior spoke in your council — we have heard his speech. For the men of Bethulia rescued him and he reported to them everything he had said before you.

**10** Therefore, O master and lord, do not disregard his word. Hold it close to your heart, for it is true: our people cannot be punished, and the sword does not prevail against them, unless they sin against their God.

**11** And now, so that my lord may not go away empty-handed and defeated, death has come upon them, and sin has taken hold of them, by which they will provoke their God to anger whenever they act wickedly.

**12** For their food ran short and all their water grew scarce, and they resolved to lay hands on their livestock and determined to consume all the things which God by his laws commanded them not to eat.

**13** The firstfruits of the grain and the tithes of the wine and oil, which they had consecrated and set aside for the priests who minister before the face of our God in Jerusalem — things which no member of the people may even touch with their hands —

**14** they have decided to consume. And they have sent to Jerusalem, since those there have also done the same, to bring back authorization from the council of elders.

**15** And when the word comes back to them and they act upon it, they will be handed over to destruction on that very day.

**16** Therefore I your servant, knowing all these things, fled from them; and God sent me to accomplish with you things that will astonish all the earth — everyone who hears of them.

**17** For your servant is God-fearing, and I serve the God of heaven day and night. Therefore I will stay with you, my lord, and your servant will go out each night into the valley and pray to God, and he will tell me when they have committed their offenses.

**18** Then I will come and report it to you, and you will march out with your entire army, and not one of them will stand against you.

**19** And I will lead you through the midst of Judea until you come to Jerusalem. I will set your throne in the midst of it. You will drive them like sheep without a shepherd, and not a dog will open its mouth before you. For this was told to me according to my foreknowledge; it was announced to me, and I was sent to report it to you."

**20** Her words pleased Holofernes and all his servants, and they marveled at her wisdom, saying,

**21** "There is no woman like her from one end of the earth to the other — so beautiful of face and so wise in speech."

**22** Holofernes said to her, "God has done well to send you ahead of the people, so that power may rest in our hands and destruction fall upon those who have held my lord in contempt.

**23** And now you are beautiful in your appearance and wise in your words. If you do as you have said, your God shall be my God, and you will live in the household of King Nebuchadnezzar and be celebrated throughout all the earth."

---

### Council Notes

**On v. 7 (the oath formula):** EMET and LOGOS render this as a solemn oath formula paralleling covenant language. PNEUMA makes it more conversational. SOPHIA retains the formal oath structure given the legal weight Judith is placing on her words.

**On v. 13 (the sacred firstfruits):** All three agents converge on "firstfruits" (aparchas) and "tithes." The detail matters theologically: what is at stake is not just food laws but sacrilege — misappropriating things dedicated to God.

**On v. 14 (gerousia):** LOGOS renders "senate," EMET "council of elders," PNEUMA "the council." SOPHIA chooses "council of elders" as the clearest rendering for general readers without importing Roman republican associations of "senate."

**On the overall irony:** Judith speaks pure double-truth throughout. She says she will lead Holofernes "to Jerusalem" — and so she will, though not in the way he imagines. She says God "sent her" — true. She says "God will accomplish things through you that will astonish all the earth" — precisely true, and fatal for him.

**On v. 19 ("not a dog will open its mouth"):** An echo of Exodus 11:7, the night of the Passover. The author signals the Exodus typology explicitly.
